levels.label: Developing
levels.description: Runs long or leans on untranslated jargon; a non-expert could not restate what the project shows or why it matters.

levels.label: Meets
levels.description: Under a minute, jargon translated on first use; a non-expert can restate the claim and why it matters.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.description: Crisp and memorable, anchored to a concrete image (the 67.5-to-100 chart, 'worse than empty'), and naturally sets up the caveat.

levels.label: Developing
levels.description: The honesty caveat is missing, or appears only after an imagined skeptic raises it.

levels.label: Meets
levels.description: The caveat (injected gap / pre-registered null / matched budget / M0 pilot) is stated unprompted and framed as a design choice.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.description: Caveat stated first and defended — why it strengthens rather than weakens the result, with the specific mitigation named.

levels.label: Developing
levels.description: The statistic, its N, or the meaning of its interval is wrong, vague, or absent; cannot say what a null would look like.

levels.label: Meets
levels.description: Reproduces the key number (to rounding) with its N and correctly reads its Wilson/Newcombe interval, including what a null would look like.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.description: Derives it from the raw counts unaided and connects it to the verdict rule (interval includes zero means null) without prompting.

levels.label: Developing
levels.description: Dodges the strongest objection, gets defensive, or concedes the project is weak.

levels.label: Meets
levels.description: Names the single strongest objection and gives an honest, specific answer grounded in the design.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.description: Pre-empts multiple probes, distinguishes what the evidence does and does not show, and never substitutes 'Claude Code did that' for understanding.
